title: Probability from a constant probability density
source: Theory S1-8.1 Quick check 1; rectangle of width a and height 1/a
stem: The continuous random variable \(X\) takes values from 0 to \({a|int}\), and its probability density is the same for every value in this interval. Find \(P(X\lt {b|int})\).

steps.name: K
steps.text_tex: The graph of the probability density is a rectangle of width \({a|int}\) and area 1, so its height is \(\dfrac{1}{{a|int}}\).
steps.note: Total area under the graph is 1.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Probability is the area to the left of b.

contexts.stem: Buses leave a stop every \({a|int}\) minutes. A passenger arrives at a random time, so the waiting time \(X\) minutes is equally likely to be anywhere from 0 to \({a|int}\). Find the probability that the passenger waits less than \({b|int}\) minutes.
A rod of length \({a|int}\) cm is cut at a random point, every point being equally likely. \(X\) cm is the distance of the cut from the left-hand end. Find \(P(X\lt {b|int})\).

title: Probability from a triangular probability density
source: Theory S1-8.1 Quick check 2; density rising in a straight line from 0 to a
stem: The graph of the probability density of a continuous random variable \(X\) is a straight line from \((0, 0)\) to \(({a|int}, h)\), and the density is zero outside \(0\le x\le {a|int}\). Find \(P(X\lt {b|int})\).

steps.name: K
steps.note: Find the height from total area 1.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The area to the left of \({b|int}\) is a triangle of height \(\dfrac{{b|int}}{{a|int}}\times h\): \(P(X\lt {b|int})=\tfrac{1}{2}\times{b|int}\times\dfrac{2\times{b|int}}{{a|int}^2}={A|sf3z}\)
steps.note: Similar triangles give the height at b.

contexts.stem: The time \(T\) hours that a task takes is modelled by a continuous random variable whose probability density rises in a straight line from 0 at \(t=0\) to its greatest value at \(t={a|int}\), and is zero outside \(0\le t\le {a|int}\). Find \(P(T\lt {b|int})\).

A continuous random variable \(Y\) has probability density zero outside \(0\le y\le {a|int}\). Inside this interval the graph is a straight line through the origin. Find the probability that \(Y\lt {b|int}\).

title: Probability as density times width
source: Theory S1-8.1 Quick check 3; area of a rectangle under the density graph
stem: For a continuous random variable \(X\), the probability density is constant and equal to \({f|raw}\) for \({lo|int}\le x\le {hi|int}\). Find \(P({lo|int}\lt X\lt {hi|int})\).

steps.name: K
steps.text_tex: The probability is the area of a rectangle of width \({hi|int}-{lo|int}={w|int}\) and height \({f|raw}\).
steps.note: Probability is area under the density graph.

contexts.note: Includes the original density 0.04 on 20 to 25, probability 0.2

contexts.stem: In a model for the lengths \(X\) mm of some leaves, the probability density is \({f|raw}\) for every length from \({lo|int}\) mm to \({hi|int}\) mm. Find the probability that a leaf has a length between \({lo|int}\) mm and \({hi|int}\) mm.

The mass \(M\) grams of an item is a continuous random variable. Between \({lo|int}\) and \({hi|int}\) the graph of its probability density is horizontal at height \({f|raw}\). Find \(P({lo|int}\lt M\lt {hi|int})\).
